definition: Spatial neural networks (SNNs) constitute a supercategory of tailored neural networks (NNs) for representing and predicting geographic phenomena.
details: They generally improve both the statistical accuracy and reliability of the a-spatial/classic NNs whenever they handle geo-spatial datasets, and also of the other spatial (statistical) models (e.g. spatial regression models) whenever the geo-spatial datasets' variables depict non-linear relations.

explainer.lead: Spatial neural networks are a supercategory of tailored neural networks built to represent and predict geographic phenomena. They matter because they raise both statistical accuracy and reliability over classic neural networks when handling geo-spatial datasets.

tiers.eli5: Ordinary neural networks ignore where things are on a map; spatial neural networks are built to pay attention to location, so their answers about geographic data come out better.
tiers.practitioner: Use them instead of a-spatial neural networks when your dataset is geo-spatial, and instead of spatial regression models when the variables relate non-linearly. A pitfall is treating geographic data as if location did not matter.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as a supercategory of tailored neural networks for representing and predicting geographic phenomena; they improve accuracy and reliability over classic (a-spatial) neural networks on geo-spatial datasets and over spatial statistical models such as spatial regression when relations are non-linear. No specific formula is given.

explainer.example: Predicting a geographic phenomenon from geo-spatial data: a spatial neural network captures non-linear relations that a spatial regression model would miss, while also improving on a classic neural network that ignores location.

usedIn.name: Classic neural network upgrade
usedIn.detail: better accuracy and reliability on spatial data
